S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Incidents presenting an ongoing or significant safety risk must be reported to affected customers within 24 hours; other confirmed thermal incidents must be disclosed to affected customers within 5 business days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved representative sample and protocol. A model with a failure rate above 5% must undergo corrective action and prompt retesting. Exceeding 5% alone does not require an automatic sales restriction; regulators may restrict sales when a model-specific assessment finds a material safety risk, considering incident evidence and remediation, and must allow a reasonable opportunity to correct and retest where safe.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must include remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 2 years after this section takes effect. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to provide the capability within 6 years, where technically feasible, and must notify owners of retrofit availability, instructions, and any limitations.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this section takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, using verified data, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying data for review. A recall is mandatory if the regulator determines the model presents a material safety risk that cannot be adequately addressed through corrective action; the regulator may require interim protective measures, customer notices, or a stop-sale where warranted.

document.section_notes: S1 is the strictest section (24h regulator reporting for every incident, 24h/5-business-day customer notices, no phase-in), binding both firms since each had unreported incidents. S2 keeps the 55 °C test and 5% limit and routes per-model failure rates to purchasers and regulators but not the general public (satisfying NW-1 and HC-1), yet exceeding 5% never forces a sales stop — a weakened consequence that shields Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S3 (24-month new-unit deadline, 6-year retrofit with a technical-infeasibility escape) and S5 (8/100k only triggers regulator review, with recall dependent on a regulator material-risk finding) fall short of their safe/acceptable bounds, while S4's 36-month built-in suppression deadline is acceptable and meets HC-2; note the S2 no-sales-stop reading is the main place the document departs from the answer key's stated acceptable range.
